thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT fired: service=redwood-inference-prod, incident=INC-78421, routed_to=redwood-inference-staging_escalation_policy :rotating_light:
Alice M.: got paged, but the summary says staging policy. did the PD mapping change after the oncall rotation?
Bob K.: acked on PD. i'm oncall (primary). i did get the notification but it went to the wrong escalation chain. investigating routes now. @Carol P. can you confirm if there was a change?
Carol P.: looking — i deployed a schedule update at 18:42 UTC but did not touch the service->escalation rules. checking automation logs.
Dave S.: fyi support has two tickets from EU customers reporting spikes in 502s and timeouts around 18:40 UTC. they referenced inference timeouts. might be related.
Eve L.: if the alert routed to staging policy, prod fallback/auto-escalation might not have fired. this could delay mitigation. Bob, can you confirm whether there were missed PD escalations for the next-level responders?
Bob K.: i saw the first page and acked, but the escalation to the infra lead didn't happen. PD shows the incident assigned to PD service "redwood-inference-staging" (same name pattern, different service id).
Alice M.: that smells like a service key collision. last week we onboarded a staging cluster with similar tags. @Carol P. any chance a tag-based rule matched wrong service?
Carol P.: found it — an automation job that maps infra tags to PD services had a regex that matched both prod and staging when the region tag was missing. i pulled the job logs:
```
# automation job snippet (pd-sync)
match: /redwood-inference-(.*)/
map_to: redwood-inference-$1
# missing region check caused staging -> prod overlap
```
Carol P.: i'm rolling back the pd-sync job to last good commit and will patch the regex.
Bob K.: temporary mitigation: i'm going to reroute the live incident to the correct escalation policy so infra leads get paged. Command in PD web UI but you can also use API:
```
curl -X PUT "https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-78421" \
 -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"incident": {"escalation_policy": {"id": "P12345", "type": "escalation_policy_reference"}}}'
```
Bob K.: done — i rerouted the incident to escalation_policy P12345 (prod-sre-escalation). infra leads pinged :bell:
incident-bot: Incident INC-78421 updated: escalation_policy changed -> P12345 (manual reroute by Bob K.).
Dave S.: monitoring dashboards show error rate starting to decline after 18:50 UTC. support queue still has a few open tickets but no new flood.
Alice M.: can we suppress future false routings for 30m while Carol patches the pd-sync job? otherwise we'll get repeats during rollback window.
Carol P.: applied a temporary suppression rule for the pd-sync automation: tag-match disabled for 30m. also pushed a fix to CI -> will deploy the proper regex in 10min.
Eve L.: thanks. please create a short runbook step in the incident doc: if automation misroutes, manual reroute + suppression is the quick path. add PD API snippet above.
Bob K.: noting oncall handoff: i'll be available for 20 more minutes then handing to @Alice M. who will cover until 21:30 UTC.
Alice M.: i picked up the handoff. monitoring and PD now looking stable. will confirm all affected incidents closed and follow up with postmortem.
Carol P.: fixed the pd-sync regex and redeployed at 18:58 UTC. test runs show correct service mapping now: only matching fully-qualified service names with region suffix.
incident-bot: Incident INC-78421 resolved by Bob K. at 19:03 UTC.
Eve L.: customer impact summary for postmortem: brief 15–18 minute impact window across EU dedicated customers, some 502s and increased latencies; mitigated once reroute applied and infra escalated. schedule 30-min postmortem for 12:00 UTC tomorrow. assign owners: Carol (root cause / automation fix), Bob (mitigation timeline), Alice (customer comms).
Dave S.: i'll draft an outbound status for affected customers and link to the postmortem when ready.
Alice M.: adding PD incident id, automation commit id and screenshots to the incident doc. closing thread here. :white_check_mark:
